subject.title: [Refactor] Gateway Session Shutdown Tracker: Bounded Memory Footprint, Configurable Timeout, and Safe Abort Signal Handling

question: Should the fixed gateway shutdown budget and session_end contract become publicly configurable and cancellable, or should follow-up work remain an internal lifecycle optimization?
rationale: The source-level concerns are credible, but public configuration, Plugin API cancellation, shutdown fallback, and force-cleanup semantics require owner intent and compatibility policy rather than a mechanical refactor decision.

options.title: Internal bounded follow-up
options.body: Measure the impact, reduce retained context, and supervise overdue work without adding configuration or changing the session_end Plugin API.

options.title: Add public cancellation controls
options.body: Introduce a documented timeout and additive AbortSignal contract with fresh-install, upgrade, shutdown-grace, and plugin compatibility proof.

options.title: Retain shipped behavior
options.body: Leave the current design unchanged unless realistic measurements demonstrate material memory or resource growth.

recommendation.title: Internal bounded follow-up
recommendation.body: Measure the impact, reduce retained context, and supervise overdue work without adding configuration or changing the session_end Plugin API.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged and directly refined the current concurrent fixed-budget shutdown semantics, making them the strongest available owner for the contract decision.
